rich_summary: Rama and Lakshmana discover the dying vulture king Jatayu, who had tried to rescue Sita from Ravana during the abduction. Gravely wounded with his wings severed, Jatayu recounts how Ravana seized Sita and fled south. Even in his final moments he offers prophetic reassurance: the time of the abduction is auspicious for recovery, and Ravana will soon perish like a fish swallowing a hook. After revealing Ravana’s lineage, Jatayu dies. Rama is overcome with grief, declaring he mourns the noble bird even more than Sita’s abduction because Jatayu sacrificed his life in loyal defense. Honoring him like a father, Rama performs full funeral rites and cremates him. The episode highlights dharma, devotion beyond species, and foreshadows Ravana’s downfall.

highlight_spans.why: Introduces the fallen Jatayu and Rama’s compassionate recognition of the bird’s sacrifice.
Jatayu reveals the central plot fact: Ravana abducted Sita and fled south after severing the vulture’s wings.
Jatayu’s prophetic assurance that Ravana will perish like a fish swallowing bait foreshadows the epic’s coming conflict.
The moment of Jatayu’s death while revealing Ravana’s lineage gives the scene emotional and mythic weight.
Rama’s grief and praise of Jatayu’s sacrifice underscore the theme of loyalty and dharma even among animals.

top_scenes.scene_text: The dying vulture king Jatayu lies bleeding on the forest floor with severed wings while Rama kneels beside him, listening urgently as the bird reveals Ravana’s abduction of Sita.
Ravana’s aerial escape southward with Sita in his grasp while the wounded Jatayu falls from the sky, his wings cut by the demon king.
Rama solemnly lighting Jatayu’s funeral pyre in the forest, honoring the fallen bird like a father as flames rise against the dark woodland.
